title: Recovery While an Appeal Is Pending — Benefit Overpayment Accounts
content:
Recovery on Benefit Overpayment Accounts is suspended only when an appeal of the overpayment determination is on record with status filed or scheduled.

## Meaning of "on record"

The appeal must appear on the Department's appeal records, with the overpayment as the record appealed and a status of filed or scheduled. A claimant's statement that an appeal has been or will be filed does not stand in for the record.

## Effect of suspension

While suspended, no offset, intercept, billing or interest is taken, and voluntary repayments are still accepted. An overpayment moves to suspended from established, from in recovery when a late appeal is accepted for hearing, or from waiver pending when an appeal of the determination is filed while a waiver is under review, in which case the appeal is decided first.

## Outcomes of the appeal

| Appeal outcome | Effect on the overpayment |
|---|---|
| Determination affirmed | Recovery resumes |
| Appeal withdrawn or dismissed | Recovery resumes |
| Determination reversed | The overpayment is cancelled: every assessed component is removed by a cancellation adjustment tied to the reversing appeal, and everything already recovered is refunded to the claimant within the refund processing days, as a refund on a cancelled overpayment |
| Modified decision lowering the overpaid amount | Carried out by cancelling the original overpayment and establishing a new one for the amount the decision leaves |

## Interpretive points

- *Hypothetical:* an appeal on record as decided does not suspend recovery; only the statuses filed and scheduled do.
- *Hypothetical:* a reversed overpayment from which USD 300.00 had been offset and USD 100.00 repaid has the full USD 400.00 refunded, and every assessed component removed.
